Patient Safety & Clinical Risk

Patient safety — goals, error prevention, reporting and a culture of safety.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • State patient safety goals
  • Describe how to prevent errors
  • Explain incident reporting and a culture of safety

In simple words

Patient safety means preventing harm to patients during care. Errors can happen — the goal is to build systems that catch them before they reach the patient.

A culture of safety encourages reporting and learning from errors rather than blaming individuals.

International Patient Safety Goals (key ones)

Goal What to do
Identify patients correctly Use two identifiers (name + ID band)
Improve communication Clear handover, read-back orders
Improve medication safety Five rights, high-alert drugs
Ensure correct surgery Mark the site, time-out
Reduce infection Hand hygiene, aseptic technique
Reduce falls Assess risk, assist mobility

Error prevention

  • Use two patient identifiers before any procedure or medication.
  • Follow the five rights of medication administration.
  • Do time-out before surgery (correct patient, site, procedure).
  • Report near misses and incidents — they reveal system weaknesses.
  • Use checklists and standard protocols.

Culture of safety

  • Report errors without fear of blame.
  • Learn from near misses.
  • Focus on system fixes, not individual blame.
  • Support open communication.

🔴 Two patient identifiers

Always use two identifiers (name and ID band) before giving medication, blood or doing a procedure. This prevents wrong-patient errors.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Identify the patient — check name and ID band before every medication, procedure or blood transfusion.
  • Hand over clearly — use SBAR; read back verbal and telephone orders.
  • Medication safety — five rights; extra care with high-alert drugs.
  • Report incidents — report errors and near misses through the incident system.
  • Fall prevention — assess risk, use call bells, assist mobility.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Patient safety prevents harm during care.
  2. Use two identifiers (name + ID band) before procedures or medication.
  3. Follow the five rights of medication administration.
  4. Do a time-out before surgery (correct patient, site, procedure).
  5. Report errors and near misses — they reveal system weaknesses.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Hand hygiene and aseptic technique reduce infection.
  2. Assess fall risk and assist mobility.
  3. Read back verbal and telephone orders.
  4. A culture of safety focuses on system fixes, not blaming individuals.

📌 Memory trick

Patient ID: “N-I” — Name and ID band. Two identifiers every time.

60-second revision

  • Patient safety = prevent harm during care.
  • Two identifiers before procedures/medication.
  • Five rights of medication; time-out before surgery.
  • Report errors and near misses.
  • Culture of safety = system fixes, not blame.

Test yourself

Before giving medication, check:

Answer: B. Use two identifiers — name and ID band — to prevent wrong-patient errors.

A near miss is:

Answer: B. A near miss is an error caught before it reaches the patient.

Time-out before surgery checks:

Answer: A. Time-out verifies correct patient, procedure and site before starting.

A culture of safety focuses on:

Answer: B. A culture of safety fixes system weaknesses rather than blaming individuals.

Incidents should be reported:

Answer: C. Report all incidents and near misses — they help prevent future harm.
